div.head: EGu Prol.
div.ab: And ðis is seo gerædnyss eac, ðe Ælfred cyng ⁊ Guðrum cyng ⁊ eft Eadward cyng (⁊ Gyþrum cyng) gecuran ⁊ gecwædon, ða ða Engle ⁊ Dene to friðe ⁊ to freondscipe fullice fengon; ⁊ ða witan eac, ðe syððan wæron, oft ⁊ unseldan þæt seolfe geniwodon ⁊ mid gode gehuhtan.

And þis is seo gerædnis eac, þe Ælfred cyng ⁊ Guðrum cyng ⁊ eft Eadward cyng (⁊ Guðrum cyng) gecuran ⁊ gecwædon, þa þa Engle ⁊ Dene to friþe ⁊ to freondscipe fullice fengon; ⁊ þa witan eac, þe syððan wæron, oft ⁊ unseldan þæt seolfe geniwodon ⁊ mid gode gehihtan.

Hoc est consilium, quod Ælfred rex et Godrún rex elegerunt et (con)dixerunt, quando Angli et Dani ad pacem et amicitiam (ad concordiam) plene conuenerunt; et sapientes etiam, qui postea fuerunt (successerunt), sepius hoc et assidue (nobis) renouauerunt et in bonum (semper) adauxerunt.

And þis is seo gerædnis eac, þe Ælfred cyng ⁊ Guðrum cyng ⁊ eft Eadward cyng (⁊ Guðrum cyng) gecuran and gecwædon, þa þa Engle ⁊ Dene to friðe ⁊ to freondscipe fullice fengon; ⁊ þa witan eac, þe syððan wæron, oft ⁊ unseldan þæt seolfe geniwodon ⁊ mid gode geiehtan.

This is also the legislation, which King Alfred and King Guthrum, and afterwards King Edward and King Guthrum, enacted and agreed upon, when the English and the Danes unreservedly entered into relations of peace and friendship. The councillors also who have been [in office] since then, frequently and often have re-enacted the same, and added improvements thereto.

Und dies ist ferner die Satzung, welche König Aelfred und König Guthrum (und späterhin König Eadward und König Guthrum fehlt Quadr.) erkoren und bestimmten, damals als Engländer und Dänen Friede und Freundschaft völlig anfingen; und die Witan auch, die später waren, erneuten oft und nicht selten dasselbe und vermehrten [es] mit Gutem.

And this is further the ordinance which King Alfred and King Guthrum (and later King Edward and King Guthrum lacking in Quadr.) chose and determined at the time when the English and the Danes fully entered into peace and friendship; and the councillors also, who came later, often and not seldom renewed the same and increased [it] with good things.
